fatal_errors: The proposed native-oxide annealing treatment does not reconstruct the reported intervention: atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating followed by a 2 h anneal, optimally at 550 °C.
The material system is Q235 steel rather than the target uncoated SS316L substrate with an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating.

No cited evidence establishes that Q235 begins with an amorphous protective iron-oxide film, that this film is the governing barrier in molten salts, or that crystallizing it by annealing improves protection.
Evidence E3 concerns titanium passivity in physiological environments and cannot support the proposed behavior of iron oxide on Q235 at 700–900 °C.
The study omits the specified acid electrochemistry, salt compositions, cyclic 900 °C exposure, coating microstructure, and critical coated/as-sprayed and uncoated references.
The annealing atmosphere, temperature, duration, and oxide-forming oxygen potential are unspecified, so the claimed oxide transformation is neither controlled nor reproducible.
explanation: The response offers a testable alternative centered on oxide-film stability and includes untreated controls, microscopy, XRD, gravimetry, boundaries, and a nominal falsification rule. Nevertheless, it has little agreement with the hidden study, whose protection arose from an APS AlCoCrFeNi coating annealed for 2 h at 550 °C on SS316L, with grain refinement, reduced defects, retained BCC/FCC phases, and Al/Cr-rich passive scales. The predicted qualitative benefit from annealing and recognition that aggressive salts can defeat oxide protection provide only weak overlap. Most importantly, the cited papers do not validate the central Q235 amorphous-to-crystalline iron-oxide mechanism. The proposed comparison also cannot cleanly isolate oxide crystallinity because annealing can alter substrate microstructure, scale thickness, porosity, stress, and chemistry simultaneously. A stronger design would independently control pre-oxidation and bulk heat treatment, measure oxide thickness/composition before exposure, include sham-annealed and oxide-stripped controls, and use the same defined salt and electrochemical conditions.
